inputs.filter: Erosion rate > 0 and Time interval > 0 for all fits

evidence_flags.flux_identity: SF>0, A>0 and |ER/(SF/A*1e6) - 1| <= 0.05 (rate constructed from a sediment budget)
evidence_flags.lock_comp: Methodology x Compilation, n>=10, >=5 distinct intervals, >=1.0 dex of logTI, IQR(log10(ER*TI)) <= 0.10 dex
evidence_flags.lock_ref: same at Methodology x Compilation x Reference level with n>=5
evidence_flags.soft_lock: same geometry with IQR(log10(ER*TI)) <= 0.30 dex (near-lock flag only)

class_assignment.coupled: ex_identity OR flux_identity OR lock_comp OR lock_ref
class_assignment.independent: not coupled AND Methodology in {Cosmogenic surface, Cosmogenic detrital, Thermochronometric}
class_assignment.indeterminate: all other rows (Volumetric / Relief without an independent flux identity)

classification_rule.notes: Reference-level locks are the strongest evidence: within one paper the same rate construction is reused while the reported interval varies, so the invariant ER*TI is an algebraic artifact rather than geology.

defensible_exponent.stratum: Glacial | Cosmogenic surface | independent class (CRN surface-exposure clocks)
defensible_exponent.why_defensible: CRN-clock rates, not product-locked by the reported interval; but the slope is shallow (-0.26 +/- 0.12) and the strata are not at the attenuation depth, so the exponent is 0 > slope > -1 rather than exactly -1.

attenuation_lock.rule: CRN stratum with median ER*TI within 0.25 dex of the ~0.6 m effective attenuation depth, IQR(log10 ER*TI) <= 0.30 dex, >=1 dex of logTI
strata: Nonglacial | Cosmogenic surface | Marrero et al., 2018
attenuation_lock.meaning: For CRN inventories E = P/(rho*(1-exp(-T/tau))); at steady state E*T -> Lambda/rho ~ 0.6 m. A CRN stratum whose ER*TI clusters at 0.6 m is therefore the same algebraic lock as thickness/interval, even with no exhumation column populated.

cannot_quote: All pooled/all-row slopes are dominated by product locks (OCTOPUS slope -0.995, R2 0.998 arises because ER*T = ~0.65 m for every row).

Glacial Thermochronometric: slope -0.577 +/- 0.111 for the whole stratum, but 47 of 68 rows share TI = 1 Ma and the 1.62 dex rate spread inside that single interval supplies all of the leverage; excluding TI == 1 Ma the slope is -0.656 +/- 0.182 (n=21), i.e. it survives but rests on 21 rows and 10 references.
Glacial Volumetric (all classes): E*T spans 9.1 dex, so the data cannot separate coupling from geology; no scaling exponent should be quoted.
conclusion.counter_case: Within Glacial | Volumetric | This study a 2.57e7 yr change in interval is accompanied by only a 1.01 dex change in rate: log10(E*T) moves 9.14 dex. Same pattern in Glacial Volumetric Hallet (7.21 dex) and Nonglacial GloRiSe (6.15 dex). Across the 19 largest strata the within-stratum slope correlates with the spread of log10(E*T) (Spearman rho = 0.62, p = 0.0044), i.e. the steeper the apparent scaling, the more tightly the product is pinned.
conclusion.summary: A steep near -1 exponent is not defensible anywhere in this compilation: every stratum that produces one is either product-locked (exhumation, flux or CRN attenuation depth) or driven by a single repeated interval. The best de-biased estimate is the glacial cosmogenic-surface stratum, where the exponent is -0.26 +/- 0.12 over ~1e2-2e5 yr, and the thermochronometric stratum, where it is -0.58 +/- 0.11 over ~1e5-2.5e8 yr but is carried by a 1 Ma cluster. Volumetric/Relief data, which span 4-9 dex of E*T, cannot separate coupling from geology and should not be quoted at all.
